Target 500 and comment completeness were not achieved. ChromeCaptureWorker was an offline importer; this agent-assisted capture was separate from earlier NativeTikTokClient 0/500 results.
nodes.norm_label: agent assisted chrome capture is not unattended crawling

nodes.label: Missing live Chrome integration diagnosis
nodes.rationale: Historical diagnostic confirmed ChromeCaptureWorker imported saved public capture and never connected to Chrome. The one-post success did not prove unattended collection. Failure to reach 500 reflected incomplete live integration, not evidence of a new TikTok block; no new acquisition or code modification occurred in this diagnostic turn.

nodes.label: Local Chrome bridge introduction
nodes.rationale: TikTokCrawler 2.4.0 introduced an authenticated localhost streaming bridge and automatic Chrome extension. An agent-driven actual run ended INTERRUPTED after 638.85 seconds with two posts, 30 comments, 13 replies and 45 unique native IDs. Extension 1.0.0 passed simulated APIs but was not installed or live-tested at this point; pairing preceded crawl timer.

nodes.label: Extension installation and pairing contract
nodes.rationale: Instructions used Load unpacked for Crawler/Backend/Tiktok/chrome_extension, an already logged-in TikTok tab, local CLI and temporary popup pairing. Pairing precedes crawl timer; CAPTCHA is manual and another debugger must not attach to the same tab. This was guidance only, with no installation or live automation performed in that turn.

nodes.label: Pairing timeout is separate from crawl time
nodes.rationale: TikTokCrawler 2.4.1 added a verified extension plan/version, connected-before-run event, waiting heartbeat and separately scoped pairing timeout. User confirmed extension installed, but first 600-second pairing wait timed out without starting acquisition; retry awaited pairing for 3600 seconds before the authorized 500-post/1800-second crawl. No new TikTok data existed yet.
nodes.norm_label: pairing timeout is separate from crawl time

nodes.label: Source pagination replaces idle completion
nodes.rationale: Historical CLI 2.5.0/native 1.2.0/extension 1.1.0 waited on source pagination and all parent replies instead of three idle rounds. The previous trial yielded 13 posts, 93 comments and 261 replies, below target 500. Crawler/preview stopped; latest fix was offline-only. Publication used a feature branch with main preserved and no Streamlit redeploy.

nodes.label: Synthetic counts are not live TikTok results
nodes.rationale: User's installed-version claim must not be contradicted without evidence. Source logs established premature idle completion. Connector 1.2.1 selected Comments explicitly and scoped replies; 1200 comments/100 replies belonged only to synthetic fixtures. Actual prior 1.2.0 trial ended with source errors at four posts, 92 comments, 52 replies. New run 6cd0ad73 started 11:25 WIB with 14:25 deadline and was ongoing, not a 1000-post success.
nodes.norm_label: synthetic counts are not live tiktok results

nodes.label: Queued keywords are not executed queries
nodes.rationale: Historical live task inherited all 25 root queries, any-match education include keywords and 40 root exclude phrases. Empty comment_exclude_keywords allowed child text without keyword matches. Sequential thread-first scheduling could stop at target/deadline before all queued queries executed; run 6cd0ad73 remained ongoing, without a success claim.
nodes.norm_label: queued keywords are not executed queries

nodes.label: Reply control starvation and forced scrolling
nodes.rationale: Source and offline tests reproduced unresponsive reply-control retries starving scroll, wrong parent keys for same-label controls and broad wrappers displacing the comment list. Connector 1.2.2 added per-control retries, correct parent/position identity and guaranteed scroll after three unproductive clicks without terminating comment collection. Historical bridge verified 1.2.2 around 11:56 WIB; completed operations were four posts, 302 comments, 363 replies, still partial.
nodes.norm_label: reply control starvation and forced scrolling

nodes.label: Clipped reply controls require visibility checks
nodes.rationale: Correction: per-control retries/forced scroll alone did not stop offscreen reply buttons from jumping back to top because getClientRects remains nonempty when clipped. Connector 1.2.3 intersected button geometry with viewport and clipping ancestors. Offline tests passed, but live bridge last verified 1.2.2 at 12:10 WIB; 1.2.3 handshake and live progress were still required.
nodes.norm_label: clipped reply controls require visibility checks

nodes.label: Unified frontend connector contract
nodes.rationale: Frontend-first source/job flow combined configuration, review, pairing and progress using a same-project, same-origin private pairing contract without fixed bridge port. Gateway/worker remained unimplemented and demo did not control real Chrome. Timer starts after verified handshake; reconnect preserves deadline; active thread counts remain separate from completed operations. Historical 13:10 live checkpoint was separate, ongoing and incomplete.
